item: M12 — the rule breaks the app already recorded, tallied for the review that reads them
issue: Rule breaks were produced and never surfaced: correction.dailyState() derived named breaches and guardrails.logEvent() had been writing blocked_attempt/override/breach/journal_record rows into guardrail_events since M64, while performance.js contained zero references to a rule break — so the weekly review could show P&L, session, grade and mistake segments and never answer “how many times did my own rules stop me this week, and which rule was it?”. The ledger's direction is aggregate, not detect.

owned_surfaces.module: src/rule-breaks.js (rule-breaks-v1): a pure evaluate() over already-read audit rows plus an inspect() that reads the trader's own accounts only, newest-first and bounded; prevented = blocked_attempt, accepted = override, observations = breach/state_observed (a CONDITION, not an attempt), records excluded = journal_record (honest history), all four kept apart on purpose
owned_surfaces.endpoint: analytics.rule_breaks on the EXISTING GET /api/analytics — no new route, scoped to the resolved analysed account (not every desk the trader owns) with from/to from the payload's own window
owned_surfaces.card: public/js/views/rule-breaks.js (Views.ruleBreaks.card) mounted in public/js/views/analytics.js above its existing tabs and loaded by public/index.html after behavior-days.js

framing_rules: an unknown read is `unavailable` with breaks:null — never zero and never a clean week; a reversed from/to range answers the same way rather than being silently widened
a prevented attempt is a refusal the app issued, an accepted override is a break that was allowed with a stated reason, and the two are counted as breaks — separately from each other
an observed live-stop CONDITION is not an attempt and is never added to the break count
legal records and closes during a stop are excluded from the count because honest history is not misconduct
a break is never joined to a result: outcome_joined:false carries the sentence saying why, and the payload carries no P&L beside the count
a row whose snapshot cannot be decoded is counted as unreadable and named; a row that named no rule is counted but not attributed to a rule it did not carry
read-only: no write, no new endpoint, and no influence on any grade, cap, permission or guardrail decision — the guardrail reads the live state, never this tally
an empty-but-readable scope answers with real zeros and by_rule:[] plus the sentence that it is a recorded tally, not a claim about unrecorded behaviour
no 70 %/causal/predictive/broker/human/mental-state/provider/production claim; nothing retuned; no existing guard weakened

carried_not_owned.why: The dependency-free minifier was delivered in its own commit (1bf6bab) on top of the M112 release, before this milestone. It is carried unchanged into every M12 stage tree and into the fixed archive so a stage measures M12's own fault rather than the absence of an unrelated tool, and its own apparatus stays frozen under analysis/evidence/jsmin/ (113/0 across six probes).

cohort_before_control_arms.note: Written before the delivered tree's final runs; the builder asserts the measured numbers from analysis/evidence/m12/feature-summary.json and each probe's own results file, so this file is the scope statement, not the evidence.
